A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SLMRec. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation experiments on four Amazon domains, efficiency measurements, ablations, and online-distillation and block-number studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original recommendation and efficiency results and reports additional baseline comparisons and revised model-study results.

M1.justification: Equation 5 changes the stated auxiliary-supervision loss from averaging over b blocks to averaging over B-1 blocks, excluding the final block. The architecture and other loss components remain equivalent after notation changes. This establishes a limited revision to the specified objective, without establishing an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate next-item recommendation on the same Amazon 2018 Cloth, Movie, Music, and Sport domains. The motivational experiments still cover Cloth and Movie; moving Movie plots to Appendix B.1 adds no coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add evaluated Caser, HGN, and LightSANs comparisons across all four domains, substantially expanding the traditional-recommender comparison set. Existing baselines remain; v2's E4SRec corresponds to v1's modified E4SRec*, rather than a newly introduced comparator.

E3.justification: Figure 4 changes the online-distillation and block-number evaluation from Music to Cloth, replacing HR@10 and NDCG@10 with HR@1 and HR@5 while retaining NDCG@5 and MRR. Main-experiment preprocessing, chronological splits, 999-negative sampling, checkpoint selection, and appendix hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The regularizer ablations are retained and redistributed from v1 Tables 2–3 into v2 Tables 4 and 8. Figure 4 replaces the Music model studies with Cloth studies addressing the same questions. Results for students distilled from 32-layer teachers disappear, reducing evidence about teacher/student depth choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The revised plots do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds three baseline result sets and Cloth model-study outcomes, while removing Music model-study outcomes, the 8←32 and 4←32 result rows, and benchmark-table @10 and average-improvement columns. Shared scores and efficiency measurements remain unchanged. A notable new comparison is Cloth HR@5: LightSANs achieves 20.32 versus SLMRec's retained 19.47.

T1.justification: New Section 6 and Appendix A introduce a simplified residual-attention recurrence, quadratic denoising objectives, two propositions, and proofs relating multilayer propagation to a single optimization step. v1 contains no corresponding theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add theoretical justification as a principal contribution, including a claim that a single-layer decoder can reproduce multilayer representations. The existing empirical claims about competitive accuracy, 13% parameters, and 6.6x/8.0x acceleration remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an optimization-based explanation of redundancy: successive layers optimize distinct denoising objectives that can allegedly be replaced by one step, with distillation transferring the resulting feature extraction capability. v1 relies on empirical observations and hypotheses about representation size, initialization, and fine-tuning. The few-shot adaptation and retraining limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a SLMRec source-code/data availability link and identifies RecBole as the implementation framework for Caser, HGN, and LightSANs. Existing hyperparameter tables, mixed-precision information, GPU specifications, and efficiency batch sizes are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction now distinguishes the work from three recommendation scaling-law studies by model scale and ranking-versus-loss evaluation. The new theory introduces graph-signal and optimization-based positioning, while related work expands to additional recommendation architectures and the newly evaluated baselines. These are substantive additions beyond the citation-style conversion.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and narrative order remain. Targeted rewrites clarify block notation and motivation; author information, terminology, and citation style change. Appendices are organized into Proof and Experiments with a contents page. A new unresolved 'Appendix??' reference remains in Related Work.

P2.justification: The combined motivational plots are redrawn as separate metric panels in Figures 2 and 5. Benchmark tables are substantially redesigned, ablations separated, and Figure 4's axes and layout revised. New ranking colors are sometimes misleading: Table 2 marks SLMRec's Cloth HR@5 of 19.47 as best despite LightSANs scoring 20.32.

improvement.justification: Additional baselines, clearer metric plots, and implementation links improve comparison and reproducibility documentation. However, v2 removes teacher-size and metric results, introduces incorrect ranking highlights, and overstates its new theoretical support: Appendix A.1 drops the gradient's factor of two between Equations 12 and 14, while the matrix-collapse argument does not establish the claimed equivalent LLaMa decoder. These substantive gains and weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
